title: WORKDAY vs NETWORKDAYS: two sides of business days
meta_desc: WORKDAY vs NETWORKDAYS: one moves a date forward by working days, the other counts working days between dates. INTL variants, holidays, off-by-one rules.
intro: Mirror twins: NETWORKDAYS answers "how many business days between these dates?", WORKDAY answers "what date is N business days from here?". Mixing them up — or forgetting their different inclusivity rules — is where deadline sheets go wrong by a day.

cols: Date + N working days → what DATE?
Date range → how MANY working days?
No — day 1 is the NEXT working day
Yes — both endpoints count if they're weekdays
Universal (executed in every LibreOffice version we test; Excel/Sheets per docs; .INTL variants Excel 2010+)

when.use_when: Computing due dates: "invoice payable 10 business days after issue" is =WORKDAY(A2,10,holidays). Negative N steps backward — "prep starts 5 working days before the event".

Measuring spans: SLA elapsed days, business days remaining in a period, working-day durations between timestamps. Remember it counts BOTH endpoints — the round trip WORKDAY(a, NETWORKDAYS(a,b)) does NOT land on b.

compat_note: Both functions and their .INTL variants execute identically across every LibreOffice version we test; Excel and Google Sheets behavior matches per their documentation. The inclusivity asymmetry (NETWORKDAYS counts the start day, WORKDAY doesn't) is identical everywhere too — it's a semantics gotcha, not a compatibility one.
